newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers agree to end 11-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers agree to end 11-day strike.

text.p: Colombian truckers struck a deal on Thursday with government and transport companies to end the 11 day strike that has paralyzed key sectors of the economy, union leader Javier Suarez said.

He said the accord granted an immediate 16 percent raise in cargo freight rates with a further index-linked increase at the start of next year. A multi-agency commission will be created to carry out a cost study of the industry and introduce possible further reforms. The strike is set to officially end at midnight (0500 GMT), Suarez said.

The breakthrough came after a day of lengthy talks involving Surez and fellow heads of the independent Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), Transport Minister Carlos Hernn Lpez, Interior Minister Horacio Serpa and transport company representatives.

The news is likely to buoy key sectors of the economy, but seems unlikely to bring instant relief to the hard-hit coffee industry. Private coffee exporters said earlier this week that even if the strike ended before the weekend there would be significant delays in exports because of the backlogs that have built up since the stoppage began at midnight October 13.

Surez said the deal should have no impact on inflation given that the 16 percent raise would be absorbed by the transport companies. He added that the deal would put truck drivers in break even position rather than operate at a loss as at present. But he said the multi-agency commission due to be set up under the agreement would have to look at ways of further boosting truck drivers' income potential.
